span.p:
greeting (per DID)
+ recording notice
always first, every call

span.p:
SKIPPED
the app said both (D48)
asking twice is bad service

div.style: color: rgb(74, 47, 0) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
did the NUMBER
say the line?

span.p:
ROUTED
line + reason -> the queue
before a word is transcribed

div.style: color: rgb(8, 54, 29) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(46, 16, 101) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p:
EXHAUSTED
line's queue if we have one,
general if we do not (D40)

div.style: color: rgb(46, 16, 101) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(36, 41, 47) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
EVERY dotted path still ends in a queue.
Not one of them hangs up on the caller.
That is the floor the AI layer sits on (D37).

div.style: color: rgb(36, 41, 47) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
AI intake runs AFTER this, while they wait.
It adds detail a keypad cannot capture.
If it fails, routing is unaffected -
it was never the AI's job.
